metadata.title: Brief von Stefan Zweig an Hannah Altmann [April 1941], SZ-AAL/B1.122

context:
## Dieses Dokument

- Titel: Brief von Stefan Zweig an Hannah Altmann [April 1941], SZ-AAL/B1.122
- Signatur: SZ-AAL/B1.122
- Datum: 04.1941
- Objekttyp: Brief
- Umfang: 5 Scans

pages.transcription:
Dear Hannah, we had your letter of the 25 April just on Lottes
birthday - she is now much better and I hope her recovery will
be a during and complete one. We have now decided not to go
to Brazil as her treatment will continue and I do not want to
expose her to new changes - on the other hand the political situation
is not clear at all and it would be risky to travel by boat. Here
we will have no difficulty to stay longer than our permit was (six
month) and we will go somewhere to the country and I hope to
work there better than here in Newyork. Here I have to write some
little things between to assure our living, I have to see some people
and to correct the English and French proofs of my book on Brazil
- when all this will be finished we want to retire ~~and not~~
more to ~~stand~~ the terrible heat here like last year (my goodness,
it is already nearly a year! and what a year!!). I do not know
if you will have heard through the wireless my ~~address~~ - I have
to say it in German for the European waves, in English for the
London radio, in English again before the public and so three
twice in the microphone, once before the eating crowd
times in one evening and it will be one of these enormous dinners
which I hate with thousand nerves; but everyone has to do his
duty and I try at least to avoid all phraseology of democracy
which will be poured over this evening by a ~~dozen~~ of other
speakers. You may imagine how we follow in the newspapers
all news about England and every air-attack let us think of you
- has Manfred already had opportunity to give his medical help?
He as a doctor will probably see more as everyone other. You should
keep a diary as it will be for coming generations an unforgettable
story - alas for us it is more sad, especially for our generation
which goes for the second time through this ordeal. Please give
Manfred my best wishes for his birthday, we are so sorry that we
cannot sit together quietly and happy and even not send him a
little present for this day. Thanks for all you have arranged with

pages.transcription:
my accountant. Mondadori was my Italian publisher but
my books have been banned already half a year before the
war, only when all this fascism will be over they will be
there printed again. I hope you have received the power of
attorney which was legalised here at the British Consulate and
which we did send by registered mail; I like to have my
things in order even in a disorderly world, it is the only
inheritance which has remained me from my father, this punc-
tuality and methodic order. - We will stay here in any case
till to the middle of June and you shall have regular news
from and about Eva who enjoys very much the stay in Croton
and is developing into a young lady out of the little child
you did send over. As to the things which I want to do for
me the first is that you buy for us - lavishly - a beautiful
birthday present to your husband as we could not do it
ourselves, secondly that you write to us if we can let you
send by ~~us~~ our friends a food parcel again and if you have
told
special wishes, I would have arranged it also for Frietental
but I do not know his new adress. Now I have talked enough
and want only to tell you that you may take out of
life what is to be taken and not to be parcimonious -
this war is now starting from this side and we do not
know how long it will take from our life. Kindest regards
to all of us. Yours
Stefan Zweig
